units.title: Opposite-order assignment minimizes the latest delivery
units.statement: For houses at distances 1,…,N and elves needing i minutes per kilometre, assigning elf i to distance N+1−i minimizes the maximum arrival time. If i<j but i is assigned the nearer of two houses a<b, swapping those assignments changes their times from ia,jb to ib,ja; both new times are at most jb. Repeating removes all same-order pairs. The optimal makespan is max_i i(N+1−i)=floor((N+1)^2/4), which is 1024 for N=63.
steps: Use a pairwise exchange to pair faster elves with farther houses
Write the arrival times as i(N+1−i)
Maximize the concave quadratic over integer i
